Defect Prevention Techniques for Repeated Defects When a project experiences repeated defects in similar modules, defect prevention techniques help identify the root causes of errors and improve the development process to avoid future defects. Defect Prevention Techniques 1. Root Cause Analysis (RCA)  RCA identifies the actual reason behind repeated defects.  Instead of fixing only the symptom, it finds the original source of the problem. Techniques Used in RCA  Cause-and-Effect (Fishbone/Ishikawa) Diagram  Pareto Analysis  Why-Why Analysis  Defect Classification Benefits  Prevents recurrence of the same defects.  Improves understanding of problem areas.

ation Benefits  Prevents recurrence of the same defects.  Improves understanding of problem areas.  Helps teams take corrective actions. 2. Benefits  Reduces defect leakage.  Improves coding standards.  Enhances software quality. 3. Benefits  Reduces inconsistencies.  Improves maintainability and reliability.

Applying V-Model in an E-Commerce Application The V-Model is a Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) model in which each development phase is associated with a corresponding testing phase. It emphasizes both Verification and Validation activities.  Verification →“Are we building the product correctly?”  Validation →“Are we building the correct product?” For an E-Commerce Application, the V-Model can be applied as follows: 1. Requirement Analysis ↔Acceptance Testing Verification  Business requirements are analyzed and reviewed.

irement Analysis ↔Acceptance Testing Verification  Business requirements are analyzed and reviewed.  Example requirements: o User login o Product search o Shopping cart o Online payment Validation (Acceptance Testing)  Customers verify whether the system meets business needs.  Example: o Check whether users can successfully place orders and make payments. 2. System Design ↔System Testing Verification  Overall system architecture is designed.  Modules like payment gateway, product management, and order tracking are planned. Validation (System Testing)  Entire application is tested as a complete system.

UNIT 2 White Box Testing — Short Note  White Box Testing checks the internal structure, logic, and code of software.  Tester has knowledge of source code.  Also called Glass Box Testing or Structural Testing.  Focuses on: o Statement coverage o Branch coverage o Path coverage o Loop testing  Performed mainly by developers.  Helps detect logical and coding errors early.  Advantages: o Improves code quality o Finds hidden bugs o Ensures maximum code coverage  Disadvantages: o Requires programming knowledge o Time-consuming Black Box Testing — Short Note  Black Box Testing checks software functionality without knowing internal code.  Tester focuses on input and output behavior.

Unit Testing vs Integration Testing — Short Note Unit Testing  Tests individual modules separately.  Performed by developers.  Finds logic and coding errors early.  Fast and simple testing. Integration Testing  Tests interaction between combined modules.  Checks interface and data flow.  Detects communication defects.  Performed after unit testing. System Testing — Short Note  System Testing checks the complete integrated software system.  Performed after integration testing.  Verifies functional and non-functional requirements.

Cause Effect Diagram  Also called Fishbone or Ishikawa Diagram.  Used to identify root causes of problems.  Problem is shown at the head; causes are shown as branches.  Helps in defect analysis and process improvement. Pareto Diagram  Bar graph based on 80/20 rule.  Helps identify major problems causing most defects.  Bars arranged in descending order.  Used for prioritizing issues and quality improvement.
